name: Masaryk University
summary: Public university in Brno with 11 English-taught bachelor's across five faculties, plus General Medicine, Dentistry and Pharmacy.

handoff.label: English-taught programmes by faculty and level

ib.text: Masaryk accepts the IB Diploma directly as proof of secondary education, with no nostrification. Each programme sets its own test, interview or documents; several waive English for IB students.

apply.via: MU e-application, one per programme and fee

dates.label: Social Studies applications open for autumn 2027

programmes.name: Biology and Biochemistry
programmes.about: Biology and biochemistry taught together: cell and molecular biology, genetics, microbiology, physiology and chemistry, with lab courses and a bachelor's thesis inside a research group.
programmes.overview: The degree covers cell and chemical biology, inorganic and organic chemistry, biochemistry, microbiology and genetics, animal and plant physiology, molecular biology and biotechnology, ecology and bioinformatics, immunology and virology. Besides lectures and seminars you take laboratory courses in biochemistry, bioanalytical chemistry and molecular biology, and take part in research for the bachelor's thesis under experienced supervisors, with training in data analysis and scientific communication. Graduates continue to master's programmes in molecular and cell biology or biochemical and cellular technologies, or work in pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries, quality control and research.
programmes.ib: Online test and online interview in biology and biochemistry; no fixed English level, upload your best proof.
programmes.selectionNote: Online test of 12 open questions, then an online interview on the subject, your letter and English; 350 of 500 needed at each stage. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Data Analytics
programmes.about: Mathematical foundations of data analysis with practical data skills, built with industry partners. Taught in combined (part-time) mode and run fully online, so you need not live in Brno.
programmes.overview: Mathematical thinking is the base here: five mathematics courses and probability and statistics sit beside programming in Python, databases, object-oriented languages and applied analytics such as machine learning, data visualisation, image processing, natural language processing, network science, big data and cybersecurity. The degree ends with a capstone project carried out as a full-time internship at an industrial partner. Electives in the last two semesters let you lean toward topics such as cloud technology or neural networks. Graduates go into research and development, modelling and data analysis, or on to master's study in mathematics, statistics or data science.
programmes.ib: Entry Trial Test of maths and logic problems (75 of 100 to pass); English B2 recommended.
programmes.selectionNote: One round: the Entry Trial Test at the faculty in Brno (online only in exceptional cases); a CV and motivation letter are mandatory. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Culture, Media and Performative Arts
programmes.about: Film, theatre, new media and culture studied as industries and practices, mixing film and theatre studies, media studies and cultural anthropology, with internships at Czech festivals and media.
programmes.overview: You combine film studies, theatre studies, media and communication studies and social anthropology, with training in ethnographic fieldwork, qualitative research, academic and journalistic writing, Central European cultural and media history, and the basics of audio, photo and video production. The programme blends academic knowledge, research training and practical experience, including internships at regional festivals and cultural institutions such as Jihlava and One World. Electives, for example on Italian cinema or screenwriting, shape your direction. Graduates go on to master's study or work in cultural management, film and television, festivals, NGOs and journalism.
programmes.ib: No English certificate if you attended an IB Diploma school for two years or more.
programmes.selectionNote: A statement of purpose and a 1,000-word essay from your own observations and interviews are scored; shortlisted applicants have an online interview.

programmes.name: English Language and Literature
programmes.about: English philology in four strands: language skills, linguistics, literary studies and cultural studies of the UK, US, Canada and Australia, ending with a thesis and a state exam.
programmes.overview: You study English grammar, linguistics, literary analysis and practical language skills together with the histories, cultures and literatures of the UK, USA, Canada and Australia. Everything is taught in English except translation courses, by Czech instructors and native speakers, with intensive courses and guest lectures. Electives range from American and British literature to African American studies, film genres and sociolinguistics, and you write a bachelor's thesis. A theatre group and a student magazine run alongside. Graduates teach English or translate, work in publishing, tourism and NGOs, or go on to master's study in literature, North American cultural studies, teacher training or translation.
programmes.ib: No English certificate if you attended an IB Diploma school for two years or more.
programmes.selectionNote: Statement of purpose, a teacher's recommendation and your English are scored; shortlisted applicants have a 15–20 minute online interview in English.

separateFrom.name: English Language for Education
separateFrom.reason: Different faculties and admissions: this is English philology at the Faculty of Arts (documents, then an interview); the other trains English teachers at the Faculty of Education.

programmes.name: Education for Diversity and Inclusion
programmes.about: Education and psychology, social education, and special and inclusive education for future educators, social workers and facilitators, with community work and a one-semester internship.
programmes.overview: The degree prepares you to work as an educator, social worker, coach or facilitator in multicultural settings, through three tracks: education and psychology, social education, or special and inclusive education. Modules include educational and developmental psychology and intercultural pedagogy. Practice starts in the first semester with observations in local schools and organisations, and in the second year you can work as a teaching assistant or tutor in disadvantaged communities. A compulsory 12-week internship abroad in the fourth semester places you in schools, NGOs or public bodies. Graduates work in education, non-profits and companies.
programmes.ib: Online interview; English at B1 (no certificate needed if your school taught in English).
programmes.selectionNote: A 10–15 minute online interview on motivation and diversity in education, scored out of 20; 12 needed. Up to 70 admitted. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: English Language for Education
programmes.about: English language, literature and culture for future English teachers, with compulsory teaching practice in real schools already in the bachelor's.
programmes.overview: The degree combines language study, the literature and culture of English-speaking countries, and pedagogical training, with reflected teaching practice in primary schools for every student. Lectures and seminars are paired with hands-on practice, and the department tries to model good language teaching in its own classes. It is a single-subject degree with required, elective and selective courses. Graduates can work as teaching assistants, teach English at language schools or in community centres, and continue to the master's in lower secondary school English teacher training, which leads to full teaching certification.
programmes.ib: English B2 certificate (IELTS 5.5, TOEFL 72 or Duolingo 90), or a school letter that you were taught in English.
programmes.selectionNote: A 10–15 minute online interview on your English and motivation to teach, scored out of 20; 12 needed. Up to 70 admitted. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

separateFrom.name: English Language and Literature
separateFrom.reason: A teacher-training degree at the Faculty of Education with its own interview and deadline; the other is English philology at the Faculty of Arts.

programmes.name: Business Management and Finance
programmes.about: Management, finance, marketing and economics for a career in business, banking or consulting, with a choice to specialise in finance or management.
programmes.overview: Taught in English, the degree covers financial accounting, financial markets and management, banking and risk, micro- and macroeconomics, leadership and human resources, mathematics, statistics and econometrics, marketing, logistics and entrepreneurship. You choose a finance track, centred on investments, accounting and corporate finance, or a management track, centred on leadership, strategy and project oversight. Learning is tied to practice through real projects, internships or related part-time jobs with international companies in Brno, and study abroad is possible. Graduates continue to master's programmes in business management or finance, here or abroad.
programmes.ib: Predicted grades don't count: take a Scio test (50th percentile) or the SAT (1050). English: IB English A or B HL at 6, or a test.
programmes.selectionNote: A final IB Diploma (28 points, Maths 4) counts only if you hold it by the deadline; otherwise a Scio GAP, OSP or Maths test. Plus a 2-minute motivation video.

programmes.name: Economics and Public Policy
programmes.about: Economics, public policy and public administration: how governments and the public sector decide, for careers in administration, international organisations, NGOs or policy work.
programmes.overview: You study how governments and the public sector work, using microeconomics, macroeconomics, statistics, econometrics and economic policy together with public administration, public economics, public policy and EU policy and institutions. Mathematics, accounting, management and academic writing in English are included, along with Czech language, and later semesters add behavioural economics, sector reforms and the economics of culture and media. Study abroad is possible through partner universities. Graduates are prepared for economic and administrative roles in public administration, international organisations, NGOs and consultancies, or for master's study.
programmes.ib: Predicted grades don't count: take a Scio test (50th percentile) or the SAT (1050). English: IB English A or B HL at 6, or a test.
programmes.selectionNote: A final IB Diploma (28 points, Maths 4) counts only if you hold it by the deadline; otherwise a Scio GAP, OSP or Maths test. Plus a 2-minute motivation video.

programmes.name: Global Challenges: Society, Politics, Environment
programmes.about: Political, social and environmental global challenges studied across political science, environmental studies, social anthropology and sociology, with training in research methods.
programmes.overview: The degree brings together political science, environmental studies, social anthropology and sociology to look at global issues, with courses on migration, environmental challenges, social movements, populism and nationalism, plus quantitative and qualitative research methods. Teaching combines lectures, seminars and practical workshops on political, social and environmental risks, and a diploma seminar in the last two semesters leads to the thesis. Internships are encouraged and can replace an optional course. Graduates work in governmental agencies, research institutions and NGOs, or continue to master's programmes in sociology, conflict studies or environmental education.
programmes.ib: Online Scio GAP test, 30th percentile minimum; IB students need no English certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Register and pay separately for Scio's online General Academic Prerequisites test and let Scio send your best result; the 30th percentile is the pass mark.

programmes.name: International Relations and European Politics
programmes.about: International relations and European politics: theories of conflict and cooperation, European integration and international political economy, with a strong thread of research methods.
programmes.overview: You study international relations theory, European integration, and the dynamics of conflict and cooperation, with regional studies of Europe, the Middle East, Asia, the Western Balkans and Arctic geopolitics, and topics such as security, human rights, diplomacy, international organisations and political economy. Research methods and academic writing build practical skills. Internships and exchange stays are accommodated, and the department has links with potential employers for elective practical training. Graduates work in diplomacy, public administration, analytical institutions, international organisations, multinational companies and journalism, or move on to the faculty's English-language master's, including the IREP programme.
programmes.ib: Documents then an online interview; IB students need no English certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Round 1 scores your cover letter, transcript and English (30 of 40 to go on); round 2 is an online interview, also 30 of 40 to be admitted.

programmes.name: Politics, Media, and Communication
programmes.about: How politics, the media and society shape each other, combining comparative politics, political theory and political behaviour with new media and mass communication research.
programmes.overview: The degree looks at how politics, media and society interact, covering how media have changed politics, their role in democracy, political communication and campaigns, and how media affect political attitudes. Foundation courses in academic writing, media studies, politics and social research methods lead to subjects such as democracy and media, populist political communication, data visualisation and public opinion, and to a two-semester bachelor thesis seminar. An optional supervised practical placement is available. Graduates work in opinion research, media, PR, public administration and political analysis, or continue in political science, media studies or political communication.
programmes.ib: Online Scio GAP test, 30th percentile minimum; IB students need no English certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Register and pay separately for Scio's online General Academic Prerequisites test and let Scio send your best result; the 30th percentile is the pass mark.

programmes.name: General Medicine
programmes.about: Six-year medical degree: two years of sciences, anatomy and physiology, then clinical rotations; Czech is taught in years 1–4 so you can talk to patients.
programmes.overview: The first two years are preclinical, with biology, biophysics, chemistry, biochemistry, anatomy, histology and physiology taught through lectures, laboratory practicals and seminars. Years three and four bring clinical introductions, microbiology, pathophysiology and summer practical training, and years four and five are clinical rotations in internal medicine, surgery, paediatrics and obstetrics and gynaecology in faculty hospitals. The last year is pre-graduation practice at clinics under experienced physicians. Graduates can practise, specialise, work in biomedical research or industry, or enter doctoral study.
programmes.ib: Tests in biology, chemistry and physics (60% to pass), or no test with 35 IB points incl. 19 from HL Bio, HL Chem and Physics.
programmes.selectionNote: Three 40-question tests; highest scores first. From Denmark you sit it via Interstudium in Oslo; EU citizens also get June and July dates. The waiver needs final grades.

lastYear.text: 2 Jan–31 July; exam via a representative

programmes.name: Dentistry
programmes.about: Five-year dental degree moving from theory through preclinical to clinical subjects, in a credit system that allows part of the study at European partner universities.
programmes.overview: The five years move from anatomy, biology, chemistry, physics and preclinical dentistry with laboratory practice, into clinical subjects such as oral surgery, restorative dentistry, prosthetics, orthodontics and periodontology, then advanced clinical work in all dental specialties alongside courses in medicine such as neurology and psychiatry. Teaching mixes lectures, seminars and extensive practical training, with professional internships from the fourth semester and a seven-week internship across dental fields in the last semester. A state exam ends the degree. Graduates practise independently, specialise, or go into academia, research or doctoral study.
programmes.ib: Tests in biology, chemistry and physics, 65% to pass; no IB waiver for Dentistry.
programmes.selectionNote: Three 40-question tests; highest scores first. From Denmark you sit it via Interstudium in Oslo; EU citizens also get June and July dates.

lastYear.text: 2 Jan–31 July; exam via a representative

programmes.name: Pharmacy
programmes.about: Five-year integrated pharmacy degree covering drug preparation, pharmacology and pharmacotherapy, and pharmacy law and ethics, with a six-month internship; over half the classes are practical.
programmes.overview: The first years teach general, inorganic and organic chemistry, cell biology, human morphology, pharmaceutical botany and physical pharmacy, then medicinal chemistry, pharmacology, pharmacognosy and toxicology, followed by clinical pharmacy, pharmaceutical technology, quality control and pharmaceutical care. More than half the classes are practical, and internships grow from two weeks to four, ending in a 20-week pharmacy internship that can be done abroad, alongside the diploma thesis. Graduates work as pharmacists, clinical pharmacists, bioanalysts, researchers or in pharmaceutical production, and can continue to doctoral study.
programmes.ib: Online biology and chemistry test (40 of 80), or none with 30 IB points incl. 11 from HL Bio and HL Chem; IB exempts from English.
programmes.selectionNote: Pick an online test date in the e-application; results within two working days. Up to 60 admitted. Waiver from the 2026/27 terms; 2027 not yet published.

notes: The Faculty of Medicine still lists a CZK 990 recognition fee before enrolment; Economics, Arts and Pharmacy charge IB holders no verification fee.
Each faculty runs its own admission and fee (CZK 800–870 per application); apply to each programme separately in the MU e-application.
Economics does not accept predicted grades as proof of academic ability, so book a Scio test or the SAT in good time.
